To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a power-recycling feeding network is proposed for the first time in a leaky-wave antenna array, and the resulting antenna array has high gain and radiation efficiency while maintaining a reasonable size in the direction of propagation.

a leaky-wave antenna array using a power- recycling series feeding network is presented, and that this antenna array achieves high radiation efficiencies and gains while maintaining a compact structure in the direction of the leaky-wave propagation.
a power-recycling LWA array is proposed and its radiation characteristics are investigated in detail.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of a novel power-recycling series feed network that can be used to efficiently drive an LWA array.
the design and analysis of the antenna array.
the design of a highly efficient leaky wave antenna array using a power recycling series feeding network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a highly efficient leakywave antenna array using a powerrecycling series feeding network was designed, fabricated and measured.
the proposed antenna is a highly efficient LWA array with a power-recycling network that achieves high gain and radiation efficiency.
a highly efficient LWA array using a powerrecycling series feeding network was proposed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a power-recycling feeding network can be used to recycle the power within the LWA array elements and completely leak out the power before reaching the terminators.
the proposed power-recycling feeding network is capable of achieving high efficiency and gain in an antenna array, while the length in the wave propagation direction is maintained to be reasonable.
a highly efficient LWA array using a power recycling series feeding network is developed, and a prototype has been fabricated and measured.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a power-recycling network can be used to improve the efficiency of an LWA array.

the proposed antenna array achieves a high radiation efficiency (greater than 80%), which is comparable to that of a conventional array fed with a Wilkinson power divider, while the length of the array in the direction of propagation is reduced by 30% compared to that of a traditional array fed with a conventional Wilkinson power divider.
a high-gain antenna with a reasonable size can be realized with the proposed power-recycling series-fed LWA array, which is a promising alternative to conventional series-fed LWA arrays.
